claims.statement: The status contract has three independent axes — a tool result's `status`, a turn's `outcome`, and an ingest's `outcome` — each with its own closed vocabulary declared in source (`nora.agent.ports.OUTPUT_STATUSES`, `nora.domain.tag_trace.VALID_OUTCOMES`, `nora.ingest.pipeline.IngestOutcome`); the words they share describe different objects and are counted on different series.

The tool-result status vocabulary is R-27's three core states (`ok`, `nothing_found`, `unavailable`) plus the named extensions in `DECLARED_STATUS_EXTENSIONS`; `OUTPUT_STATUSES` is the union derived from those two structures, and it is the single source read by both the runtime contract validator and the structural tests.

A native tool result that fails its declared output contract is REPLACED with `MALFORMED_RESULT` (`status="unavailable"`, `reason="malformed_result"`) rather than forwarded, while an exception raised by the tool still propagates untouched so a crash is not converted into a quiet `unavailable`.

`contract_violation` is deliberately mechanical: it checks that the result is an object, carries its contract's required keys, and that `status` is a member of `OUTPUT_STATUSES`; it cannot and must not judge whether a `refused` was truly a disclosure veto or a lazy `unavailable`, so semantic misuse of the vocabulary stays with tool authors and the R-27/R-31 tests.

`load_transcript` is the one deliberately status-free data tool: it answers `{"messages": [...]}` on both paths and declares the `messages` contract instead of `three_state`, because validating it against a required `status` key would turn every successful call into `unavailable`.

MCP tool groups are appended by the registry after `adapt()` runs and are deliberately not validated by the output-contract seam in this pass (ADR 0008 §5), so a status outside `OUTPUT_STATUSES` can still reach the model across an MCP boundary.

The computer's result vocabulary is a fourth state on the same axis — `SandboxStatus` is `ok` / `nothing_found` / `denied` / `unavailable` — where `denied` means refused as asked (a path outside the workspace, an ambiguous edit, an oversized body, a bad token), and a command that exited non-zero is still `ok` with its `exit_code` saying how it went.

`ComputerCallObserver.call(op, status, answered)` keeps "computerd answered `unavailable`" apart from "nothing usable came back": only an unanswered call drives `nora_computer_up` to 0, so a computer that reports unavailable is reachable while a refused, timed-out or 401 call is an outage.

A tag turn's outcome is one of six values validated at the `TagTrace` dataclass boundary (`send_reply`, `recovered`, `silent`, `vetoed`, `timeout`, `llm_error`), and the `nora_engagement_outcomes_total` vocabulary is derived from that set plus `"unattributed"`, which is not a turn outcome but the `trace is None` case.

The engagement pipeline owns the outcome value: `invoke.run` returns a provisional outcome and stamps `timeout`/`llm_error` on its own not-ok path via `_blank_trace`, while on the ok path the pipeline derives the real outcome from `delivered` and `deliverer.called` (`recovered` or `send_reply` when delivered, `vetoed` when a send was attempted and blocked, `silent` when the send tool was never called).

The shared decision log records three verdicts — `replied`, `silent`, `failed` — with `reason` holding the finer turn outcome, so a turn that chose not to speak is logged as restraint rather than as a failure; `DecisionVerdict` is a closed `Literal` covering all writers.

Ingest outcomes are a closed `Literal` of sixteen values (`scope_refused`, `audit_refused`, `sender_not_allowed`, `engaged`, `recorded`, the six `edit_*` endings, two `reaction_*` and three `delete_*` endings) that is both the span attribute vocabulary and `nora_ingest_outcomes_total`'s label set; because `make gate`'s mypy does not reach `nora/ingest`, an unknown value is logged as a warning and recorded anyway rather than withheld.

Deliberate silence on the participation occasion is counted as the healthy outcome on `nora_participation_silence_total` and never on `nora_silent_failures_total` (whose every reason is a malfunction); the gate is `ok=True and stop_reason not in BUDGET_STOP_REASONS`, so a turn a token or turn cap cut off before it could decide is an ordinary silent failure with `audience="participation"`.

R-5's silence has exactly one typed exception: `FailureClass.REQUESTED_TOOL` is `disclosable` while `INFRASTRUCTURE` and `GUARD_VETO` are silent, and `NoraError` defaults to `INFRASTRUCTURE` so an uncategorised failure defaults to silence.

The Relevance Gate resolves every non-answer to NO-GO but keeps "the model said no" apart from "I could not ask": `GateVerdict.source` distinguishes `model` from `fail_closed`, only a real verdict moves `nora_relevance_gate_total`, and `nora_relevance_gate_errors_total` carries one label per distinguishable failure kind from `GATE_ERROR_KINDS`.

The Dreamer finishes a run as `unavailable`, never `nothing_found`, when no sample's model response is readable — a timeout, an exception or a missing envelope comes back as `None` and is counted per sample — and that is the only run status that holds the watermark; a store timeout, an adaptor raising out of `accept`/`commit`, and `AccountNotRecordableError` take the same held path, leaving both the watermark and the schedule's `last_fired_at` unstamped so the next tick retries the same evidence.

Every non-`ok` tool result must carry a short English `note` explaining how to read or report that status, enforced by a static AST gate over the modules tool results are assembled in (with a positive control) and by a per-tool Level 3 check over every return of each three-state tool.

The `UnavailableOutcomes` alert is derived rather than hand-written — it fires on any `*_total` carrying `status="unavailable"` — and deliberately excludes `nora_computer_calls_total`, which has its own thresholded rule (`ComputerCallsFailing`) so one computer call cannot page twice.

A labelled Prometheus series does not exist until its first increment and `increase()` over a series whose first sample is already 1 reads 0, so `ComputerMetrics.prime()` creates every `(op, status)` of `nora_computer_calls_total` and every `(tool, stage)` of the should-be-zero `nora_computer_audit_failures_total` at zero on start-up.

A transcript window that could not be read answers `unavailable`, never `nothing_found`, because `EngagementContext._recent` returns `()` for a failed store read as well as for an empty one (R-82); the named test also pins that one tool call records exactly one of the three states, never two of them on one event.

Bounded reads are only half-closed by `nora_bound_truncated_total`: the counter fires inside the store so an operator sees that a cap bit, but the clipped tool result is still handed to the model as `ok` with no hint that its list was a ceiling — model-facing calibration is per-site render work that has not shipped class-wide.

The memory index's search status is its own four-value vocabulary (`ok`, `nothing_found`, `partial`, `unavailable`), where `partial` means the index is being rebuilt, its projection queue is not empty, or the search fell back to the lexical seed — so what was not found may still exist, and an unfinished index is never `nothing_found`.

Paths whose failure modes are finer than the core three keep their own narrower vocabulary while honouring the same separation: `nora_speech_transcriptions_total` uses `ok` / `error` / `timeout` / `unsupported` / `empty`, keeping `empty` (a legitimate 200 with no words) apart from `error` so an operator can tell an outage from an ordinary silent note.

Readability alone does not make a Dreamer run succeed: unreadability takes a run `unavailable` only when every sample was unreadable — a per-sample `asyncio.wait_for` timeout, an exception or a missing envelope returns `(None, stop_reason)`, is counted `nora_dream_sample_total{status="unavailable"}` and skipped while the loop continues — whereas a run with a readable sample behind it still ends `unavailable`, watermark held and `last_fired_at` unstamped, if `accept` raises, `commit` faults, or `AccountNotRecordableError` is raised, so the run-level status alone cannot show that one sample of several failed.

`nothing_found` on a Dreamer run has exactly two producers — a blank `inputs`, which is the general fire condition and still calls `commit(key, ())` so time-driven decay is not lost, and a run whose readable samples produced no items, proposals or writes — and neither is an outage, so reporting `unavailable` in either place would hold a watermark over a batch that was genuinely empty.

`nora_dream_store_timeout_total{phase}` exists because `nora_dream_run_total{status="unavailable"}` is also what an unreachable provider produces: only the runtime's own `asyncio.timeout` firing, confirmed by `cm.expired()`, is counted, with `phase` naming the `inputs` render or the `commit`, so a wedged store is separable from a provider refusing and a collaborator's own `TimeoutError` cannot put a false reading on the series.
